---
title: "Robustness checks for an EBMF fit"
description: "Eight runnable checks, each mapped to one exported function, before you trust a factor."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

Run these checks before you give a factor a biological name. Each one is a
short chunk on one simulated fit, with what a bad result looks like. The
checks do not replace replication across donors or datasets.
[Get started](first-fit.html) defines view, activity and effects.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

```{r simulate}
library(flashier.utils)
set.seed(17)
activity_truth <- cbind(c(rep(3, 12), rep(0.3, 12)), c(rep(0.3, 12), rep(3, 12))) +
  matrix(runif(48, 0, 0.4), 24, 2)
effect_truth <- cbind(c(2, 1.7, 1.4, 1.1, -0.6, -1.2, rep(0.1, 6)),
                      c(rep(-0.15, 6), 2, 1.7, 1.4, 1.1, -0.8, -1.2))
X <- tcrossprod(activity_truth, effect_truth) + matrix(rnorm(288, sd = 0.1), 24, 12)
dimnames(X) <- list(sprintf("s%02d", 1:24), sprintf("g%02d", 1:12))
metadata <- data.frame(sample = rownames(X), donor = rep(sprintf("d%02d", 1:12), each = 2),
                       group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 12))
fit <- fit_ebmf(X, "rows", max_factors = 4, S = 0.1, var_type = 0L,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_normal),
  backfit = TRUE, nullcheck = TRUE, seed = 1, verbose = 0,
  feature_scale = "simulated_intensity", independent_unit = "donor")
view <- standardize_factors(fit, prior_support = c(activity = "nonnegative", effects = "signed"))
```

## 1. Did the optimizer finish, and does the rank ceiling bind?

```{r convergence}
c(rank = fit$n_factors, max_factors = 4, elbo = fit$elbo,
  maxiter_reached = isTRUE(flashier::flash_fit(fit)[["maxiter.reached"]]))
factor_pve(fit)
```

Bad signs: `maxiter_reached` is `TRUE`, a native warning about convergence,
or `rank` equal to `max_factors`. A fit at the ceiling has not chosen its
rank; raise `max_factors` and refit. Tiny PVE factors are candidates for
noise, not automatically wrong. Keep the native warnings; do not rerun until
they disappear.

## 2. Does another seed find the same programs?

```{r seeds}
fit2 <- fit_ebmf(X, "rows", max_factors = 4, S = 0.1, var_type = 0L,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_normal),
  backfit = TRUE, nullcheck = TRUE, seed = 2, verbose = 0,
  feature_scale = "simulated_intensity")
agreement <- factor_replicability(fit, fit2, min_congruence = 0.9)
agreement$matches[, c("reference_factor", "target_factor", "congruence", "status")]
```

`factor_replicability()` matches factors by Tucker congruence of their
effect vectors with one-to-one assignment. Bad signs: an `unmatched_reference`
row, or congruence below your threshold for a factor you plan to interpret.
Seed agreement is initialization sensitivity on fixed data. It does not
show the program survives a change of cells.

## 3. Is a factor carried by a handful of samples?

```{r concentration}
A <- factor_activity(view)
effective_n <- colSums(A)^2 / colSums(A^2)
top5_share <- apply(A, 2, function(a) sum(sort(a, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]) / sum(a))
round(rbind(effective_n, top5_share), 2)
```

Effective sample count is `(sum a)^2 / sum a^2` for nonnegative activity.
Bad signs: an effective count near 1 to 3, or most activity mass in five
samples. Such a factor can match well across seeds and still vanish when
those samples are left out, which is what the EBMF versus cNMF case study
found for its rare HLA/CD74 factors.

## 4. How wide is the conditional uncertainty?

```{r uncertainty}
head(factor_uncertainty(fit, side = "effects", representation = view), 4)
factor_intervals(fit, side = "effects", representation = view, factors = "F1",
                 ids = c("g01", "g05", "g07"), nsamp = 200, seed = 3)
```

Posterior standard deviations and intervals are conditional on the
estimated priors and on the fitted rank. Mean-field intervals are typically
too narrow. Bad signs: an interval that crosses zero for an effect you want
to call, or `prob_zero` near one. Good signs here do not substitute for
regression standard errors or biological replication.

## 5. Do the programs survive leaving donors out?

```{r stability, eval=requireNamespace("psych", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("clue", quietly = TRUE)}
stability <- factor_stability(X, fit, metadata, unit_col = "donor", seed = 4, B = 8,
  scheme = "subsample", fraction = 0.75, min_congruence = 0.9)
stability$summary[, c("factor", "n_successful", "recovery_rate", "median_congruence",
                      "q025_congruence")]
```

`factor_stability()` refits on resampled biological units and reports how
often each reference factor is recovered. Use `scheme = "subsample"` so no
duplicated rows bias the empirical Bayes priors. Bad signs: a recovery rate
well below one, a low 2.5% congruence quantile, or failed replicates. Eight
replicates illustrate the call; use tens to hundreds for a real estimate.

## 6. Does a different prior tell the same story?

```{r priors}
fit_other <- tryCatch(fit_ebmf(X, "rows", max_factors = 4, S = 0.1, var_type = 0L,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_point_normal),
  backfit = TRUE, nullcheck = TRUE, seed = 1, verbose = 0,
  feature_scale = "simulated_intensity"), error = conditionMessage)
if (is.character(fit_other)) fit_other else
  factor_replicability(fit, fit_other, min_congruence = 0.9)$matches[,
    c("reference_factor", "target_factor", "congruence", "status")]
```

A program that only appears under one prior family is a modelling choice,
not a finding. A prior whose optimizer fails on your data is also a result:
record the message rather than retuning until it passes.
[Compare priors](compare-priors.html) shows the full workflow with known
truth and held-out prediction.

## 7. Does the noise model change the factors?

```{r noise}
fit_genewise <- fit_ebmf(X, "rows", max_factors = 4, S = 0.1, var_type = 2L,
  ebnm_fn = list(ebnm::ebnm_point_exponential, ebnm::ebnm_normal),
  backfit = TRUE, nullcheck = TRUE, seed = 1, verbose = 0,
  feature_scale = "simulated_intensity")
c(pooled = fit$n_factors, genewise = fit_genewise$n_factors)
factor_replicability(fit, fit_genewise, min_congruence = 0.9)$matches[,
  c("reference_factor", "target_factor", "congruence", "status")]
```

`var_type = 0` pools one residual variance; `2` estimates one per feature
and lets high-variance features absorb their own noise. With a supplied
`S`, the estimated variance is added to `S^2`. Factor order can swap, as
here; the matching handles that. Bad signs: a rank change, or a factor with
no accepted counterpart. Report which setting you used.

## 8. Does metadata explain it, and on the right unit?

```{r metadata}
summarize_factor_activity(view, metadata, by = "group", unit_col = "donor")[,
  c("group", "factor", "n", "n_units", "mean", "sd")]
tryCatch(test_factors(view, metadata, formula = ~group, engine = "lm",
                      unit_col = "donor", independence = "independent"),
         error = conditionMessage)
```

Group summaries are descriptive. Two samples share each donor here, so an
independent-unit test on 24 samples is refused rather than run. Bad signs:
`n` much larger than `n_units`, or a p-value from an independent engine on
repeated samples. Use the `dream` engine with the donor as a random effect,
or aggregate to one row per unit first.

```{r dream, eval=requireNamespace("variancePartition", quietly = TRUE)}
test_factors(view, metadata, formula = ~ group + (1 | donor), engine = "dream",
             unit_col = "donor", independence = "repeated")$table[,
  c("factor", "term", "estimate", "p.value")]
```

Held-out prediction on donors is in [Compare priors](compare-priors.html).

## Checklist

1. Converged, rank below the ceiling, warnings recorded.
2. Same programs across seeds, priors and noise models.
3. Effective sample count well above a handful.
4. Intervals exclude zero for effects you name, with the underdispersion caveat.
5. Recovery rate across unit resamples close to one.
6. Metadata association on the independent unit, not on repeated samples.
